To understand the concept of relativity, imagine time as a river. In our everyday lives, this river flows at a steady, predictable pace for everyone. However, Einstein’s theory of relativity suggests that this river can speed up or slow down depending on how fast you are moving or how strong the gravity is around you.

Think of it like this: Imagine you are running on a treadmill that is moving incredibly fast, almost as fast as light. To you, everything feels normal—you can talk, walk, and even sip your coffee without any issues. Your watch ticks at its usual pace. But to someone standing still outside the treadmill, it would look like you are moving in slow motion. Your watch would appear to be ticking much slower than theirs. This is because time itself is stretching out for you due to your high speed.

Similarly, gravity can also affect time. Imagine gravity as a heavy blanket. The heavier the blanket (stronger gravity), the more it pulls on time, making it pass more slowly. So, if you were near a massive object like a black hole, time would pass much slower for you compared to someone far away from it.

In summary, time is not a fixed, unchanging entity. It can stretch and shrink depending on how fast you are moving and how strong the gravitational forces are around you. This is the essence of relativity.
